summary: This bill expands the work opportunity tax credit to cover wages for hiring specified veterans to work in renewable energy, defining eligible veterans as those with military credentials in renewable energy or related skills, recent vocational degrees in the field, or LEED certification.

scores.thoughts: The bill expands an existing tax credit (WOTC) for employers, creating a new tax expenditure targeted at renewable energy hires. Tax credits function as government spending through the tax code, so this expands such spending.
The core provision amends IRC section 51 to create a new category of WOTC eligibility for specified veterans in renewable energy, directly reducing tax liability for qualifying employers.
No provisions address healthcare coverage, providers, insurance, or public health programs.
No provisions relate to firearms, background checks, or gun regulations.
No provisions address visas, border security, asylum, or immigration pathways.
No provisions address reproductive health services or abortion access.
The bill references veterans and DoD credentials but does not alter defense budgets, procurement, or military operations.
The tax credit is explicitly limited to 'fields of renewable energy' (defined to include solar, wind, etc.) and LEED certification, creating a direct incentive for renewable energy employment.

The bill supports veteran employment through a hiring tax credit, which has a tangential connection to veteran support programs but does not modify SNAP, TANF, unemployment insurance, or other core welfare entitlements.
The bill references vocational degrees and credentials as eligibility criteria but does not fund schools, alter federal education policy, or address school choice.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, incarceration, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export rules.
By expanding a tax credit, the bill increases federal revenue loss and therefore the deficit; it does not include offsetting spending cuts or debt-reduction measures.
No provisions address LGBTQ protections, nondiscrimination rules, or related legal status.
No provisions address foreign assistance, international aid programs, or State Department funding.
No provisions address voting access, election administration, or campaign finance.
No provisions address data privacy, technology regulation, or surveillance.
The bill provides an employer-side tax incentive for hiring but does not alter collective bargaining rights, union organizing rules, or worker protections.
No provisions address religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or conflicts between religious liberty and antidiscrimination laws.

The bill expands the work opportunity tax credit to cover wages paid to certain veterans hired in renewable energy fields, creating a new uncosted tax expenditure. This reduces federal revenue without any offsetting spending cuts or revenue raisers, thereby increasing the deficit.
